subject: [PATCH v4 10/13] mm/collapse: open-code collapse_single_pmd() in its two callers

2026-09-28.patch_summary: This patch removes the collapse_single_pmd() function and instead open-codes its logic in two callers, khugepaged and madvise_collapse(). The function was previously handling lock management differently for each caller, which is now handled directly by each caller. This change simplifies the code and prepares it for moving madvise_collapse() out of khugepaged.c.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David questioned whether keeping the mmap lock locked is necessary, suggesting a single collapse_single_pmd() function that always returns with the mmap lock unlocked, even if it means dropping and re-acquiring the lock multiple times.

The reviewer noted that the comment in the patch description about collapse_single_pmd() dropping the lock on some paths and not others is no longer accurate, as the function now always drops the lock before calling collapse_run_pmd(). The reviewer suggests reverting this change to maintain consistency with the original behavior.

2026-10-01.patch_summary: This patch refactors the collapse_single_pmd() function by open-coding its behavior in its two callers, khugepaged and madvise_collapse(). The original function handled different lock behaviors for these callers, but since they already act on dropping the lock, it's more straightforward to handle this directly in each caller. This simplifies the code and prepares for future changes, such as moving madvise_collapse() out of khugepaged.c.
